# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**To:** Louisiana Healthcare Connections
Appeals and Grievances Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:** Cameron Novak
Member ID: W322775483
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**Date:** [Date I am sending this letter]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated August 15, 2026 — Reference number POC-CD20076A7A-66146**
**Member:** Cameron Novak | **Member ID:** W322775483
**Service denied:** Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446
**Governing policy:** Evolent CG 1763 Knee Arthroplasty — https://ldh.la.gov/assets/medicaid/MCPP/06-12-2026/1882-LHCC-ECG-1763-for-Knee-Arthroplasty-2026-redline.pdf

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization for a partial knee replacement (CPT 27446). The notice dated August 15, 2026 states that the request does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and approve the surgery. My surgeon, Dr. Duval, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed.

I am submitting this appeal within the timeframe stated in the notice: my appeal must be received by February 11, 2027. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. If there is a different or additional way the plan needs me to submit this appeal, please contact me at the phone number above and I will do so promptly.

## The plan's own criteria, and what my records show

The policy that governs this request is **Evolent CG 1763 Knee Arthroplasty**. Below I quote the plan's own language and set my records beside it. Where an excerpt I have ends in a colon, the policy goes on to list further conditions that were not reproduced in the material available to me; I am not attempting to restate those, and I ask the plan to identify them (see my request below).

**1. The framework the plan applies.** The policy states:

> "Medial or lateral UKA/PKA may be medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria are met):"

I am asking the plan to walk through that list against my chart, because on the points I can see, my records line up.

**2. Duration and location of pain.** The policy states:

> "At least 12 weeks of pain localized to the medial or lateral compartment"

My records document **14 months of progressive pain in the knee, unrelieved by rest**. Imaging on June 29, 2026 localized the disease to the **medial compartment**, with full-thickness cartilage loss there. Fourteen months is well beyond the twelve weeks the plan requires.

**3. Non-operative treatment.** The policy states:

> "Unless bone-on-bone articulation is present, failure of at least 12 weeks of non- operative treatment, including at least TWO of the following (4,5):"

Two points are relevant here.

First, the plan's own sentence begins with an exception: the twelve-week non-operative requirement applies *unless bone-on-bone articulation is present*. My imaging of June 29, 2026 documents **full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition**. That is the exception the plan itself wrote into this criterion.

Second, even setting the exception aside, my records show substantial failed conservative care, including more than one of the categories the plan names:

- > "Physician-supervised exercise program (including home exercise program)"

  I completed **supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, 24 visits from April 28, 2026 to June 23, 2026**, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

- > "Pharmacologic treatment: oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, or analgesics"

  I took **NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief**.

- > "Injections: corticosteroid or viscosupplementation"

  I had a **corticosteroid injection on April 12, 2026, which gave only 2 weeks of partial relief**.

That is three of the plan's listed categories, not two. My physical therapy course ran eight weeks rather than twelve; my medication trial ran six months, and my pain has continued for fourteen months. I would ask the reviewer to weigh that record against the plan's own bone-on-bone exception rather than against the eight-week PT figure alone.

**4. Imaging.** The policy states:

> "Weight-bearing radiographs demonstrate only unicompartmental disease (with or without patellofemoral involvement), described as Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or grade 4 degeneration"

and it adds:

> "NOTE: MRI should not be the primary radiographic test used to determine the presence or severity of arthritic changes in the joint (9)"

I want to be straightforward about this. The imaging in my packet is an **MRI dated June 29, 2026**, which found **full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 degeneration medially**. The severity and the single-compartment location the policy asks about are therefore documented, and documented at grade 4 — the most advanced grade the criterion names. If the reason for denial is that the plan wants this shown on weight-bearing radiographs rather than on MRI, I ask the plan to say so plainly in its response. **I am willing to obtain weight-bearing radiographs, and I ask that the plan hold my appeal or issue a conditional approval on that basis rather than deny the surgery outright**, since the underlying disease the criterion describes is already documented.

**5. Timing since injection.** The policy states:

> "No corticosteroid injection into the joint within 12 weeks of surgery (1,10–13)"

My only documented corticosteroid injection was on **April 12, 2026**. That is more than twelve weeks before any surgical date that could now be scheduled.

**6. Prior arthroscopy.** The policy states:

> "No prior arthroscopic knee surgery within 6 months of surgery (14–16)"

The clinical summary submitted with my prior authorization does not describe any prior arthroscopic knee surgery. If this criterion is part of the basis for the denial, I ask the plan to say so, and Dr. Duval can confirm my surgical history in writing.

**7. Examination measurements.** The policy states:

> "Total arc of motion (goniometer) > 90 degrees (20)"

> "Contracture ≤ 10 degrees upon physical exam (goniometer) (22)"

> "Angular deformity ≤ 150 degrees, passively correctable to neutral upon physical exam (goniometer) (20)"

> "Normal anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) or stable reconstructed ACL per physical exam test (20,21)"

My chart documents **positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain**. It does not, in the summary I have, record goniometer numbers or an ACL examination result. If the denial rests on any of these four measurements, I ask the plan to identify which one, and **Dr. Duval can provide the goniometric measurements and ligament examination findings** on request. A missing measurement that was never asked for is not the same as a criterion that has been failed.

**8. Criteria that do not apply to my request.** The policy states:

> "ALL requests for simultaneous bilateral partial knee replacements should clearly indicate why simultaneous UKA is preferable to staged procedures."

> "Associated risks with simultaneous bilateral partial knee replacements should also be discussed with the patient and documented in the medical record (17,18)"

My request is for a single knee, the **[left/right — as documented in Dr. Duval's operative request]** knee, so these bilateral provisions do not apply.

The policy also states:

> "All requests for UKA in individuals with chronic, painless effusion and extensive radiographic arthritis will be evaluated on a case-by-case basis."

My pain is neither chronic nor painless in that sense — my records document fourteen months of progressive pain, inability to climb stairs without assistance, and waking three to four times a night from pain.

## Please send me the criteria the plan actually applied

The denial notice says the decision was made "under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria" but does not tell me which criterion I failed or why. **The plan holds those criteria, and I am asking the plan to provide them to me in writing as part of this appeal** — specifically, the complete criteria set the reviewer applied to CPT 27446, including the full text of any list that the excerpts above introduce but do not reproduce, and a criterion-by-criterion statement of which ones my records were found not to meet.

I understand the plan uses Evolent for musculoskeletal surgery review and that Evolent publishes these criteria openly, without a login. I am not asking for anything confidential — only for the same document the reviewer used, so that I can respond to the actual reason for the denial rather than guess at it.

## What I am asking the plan to do

1. Overturn the denial of CPT 27446 and authorize the partial knee replacement recommended by Dr. Duval.
2. If the plan does not overturn the denial, identify in writing the specific criterion or criteria in **Evolent CG 1763 Knee Arthroplasty** that my records were found not to satisfy, and state what documentation would satisfy them.
3. If weight-bearing radiographs or goniometric measurements are what is missing, tell me that, and allow me to submit them rather than close the request.
4. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician in orthopedic surgery, or in a same or similar specialty, who was not involved in the original determination.

I have been in pain for fourteen months. I have done the physical therapy, taken the medication, and had the injection, and my knee has continued to get worse. I am asking the plan to look again at the whole record.

Thank you for your time and reconsideration.

Sincerely,

**Cameron Novak**
Member ID: W322775483
Reference number: POC-CD20076A7A-66146
Date of birth: [My date of birth]
Signature: ______________________
Date: ______________________

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of the denial notice dated August 15, 2026
- Physical therapy discharge note (24 visits, April 28, 2026 – June 23, 2026)
- MRI report dated June 29, 2026
- Office notes from Dr. Duval, orthopedic surgery
- [Any additional records I am including]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
